status: Numerical, conservation, restart and memcheck validation passed; exclusive-GPU repeated 8^3/16^3 dry timing completed. Reacting boundary-layer performance remains a limitation.

baseline.role: Accepted layer-one interface migration with CPU material computation.

mathematics: Original first-order independent reaction clocks, shared extent limiter, ordered Darcy/ALE/species diffusion and accepted gas packets are retained.

When a common reaction extent mathematically exhausts its controlling donor, that donor is assigned exact zero. This removes a negative roundoff residue while retaining the original extent, other species and energy; tied controls and nonlimiting tiny inventories are tested on CPU/CUDA.
Ordered packet accumulation emulates the original x86 binary80 64-bit significand before narrowing, including the original negative-donor roundoff bound.
Whole-window backward-Euler native OpenFOAM conduction remains unchanged until layer three. Geometry and its host inventory mirror remain pending layer five.
Independent source-variation history samples are batched within bounded temporary storage. Their constitutive math, physical time interval and sequential result checks remain unchanged.

reaction_surface.scope: Eight reaction variants on 257 cells and five wall/material variants with permuted owners, inactive faces and private workspace reuse. Existing CPU stagnation cases are parity evidence, not a claim of converged closure.

transport.scope: Ns=2/3, host/CUDA against preserved 88bc implementation; eight scenarios plus failure-order and workspace-reuse checks, zero observed field differences.

packet_wide.scope: Ns=2/3; 37 ordered packet batches each, binary80 host/CUDA arithmetic, subnormals, overflow, cancellation, negative-donor bounds and original failure semantics.

backend_commit_and_history.scope: Real resident backend: rejected and uncommitted updates preserve inventory, cumulative transfers and host outputs; nine independent history samples equal sequential surface calls, including an inactive first face.

audit.scope: Closed inventories, signed interface mass/energy, and dry-case stoichiometric yields/progress; source-rate CPU/GPU parity is covered separately by kernel oracles.

performance_status: Exclusive-GPU five-pair dry medians: 8^3 5.74 to 4.37 seconds (1.3135x), 16^3 69.37 to 62.98 seconds (1.1015x). All 24 warmup/timed runs passed audits. Reacting-SST is slower at four and 64 interface faces; no universal speedup is claimed.

experiments.name: all-fast-compile
experiments.finding: All four native cases exactly match, but surface root solves are slow; mixture surface kernels account for 5.31 seconds. Replaced by production optimization for the separate material translation unit.

experiments.name: standard-material-unbatched
experiments.finding: Four exact native matches. Dry-case exploratory elapsed time falls from 47.09 to 3.37 seconds but remains slower than the CPU baseline.

experiments.name: bounded-history-batching
experiments.finding: Five native cases plus both boundary-layer models and SSPRK3 match bitwise. Dry-case exploratory time is 1.20 seconds. Small reacting-SST case is 194.27 versus baseline 37.50 seconds; this regression is not concealed.

experiments.name: temperature-device-noinline
experiments.finding: No useful register/stack reduction; source annotation removed. Other GPU work overlapped the later exploratory run, so it is not a controlled timing comparison.

experiments.name: hardware-work-count-launch-spreading
experiments.finding: Exclusive GPU two-window reacting-SST probe matches bitwise but remains slower (11.52 s baseline, 47.29 s candidate). The simpler, already validated 32-thread launch layout is retained.

Final restart output matched bitwise, but the initial validation helper incorrectly applied a nonreacting per-species conservation check to dry pyrolysis. Replaced with the existing reaction-aware stoichiometric audit; no numerical tolerance changed.
Outer Python SIGSEGV before one timing was persisted. Entire incomplete timing cohort excluded. New durable GNU-time cohort stores every solver status/time separately from isolated audits.

Input preparation retained empty mesh patches despite the existing fixture requiring slip side fields. Restored the original three-dimensional-side fixture preparation and ran a new separate cohort; solver math unchanged.

limitations: Native gas backend uses matched fast-compile=max while the separate material backend uses standard optimization with fmad=false and relaxed constexpr. This is not a fully production-optimized end-to-end benchmark.

Reacting boundary-layer GPU root solves remain slower: original four-face probe 37.50 to 194.27 seconds; exclusive 64-face single-pair probe 60.66 to 79.74 seconds. Further general-path optimization is needed; no case-specific CPU path or fallback is introduced.
Third through fifth migration layers are not implemented.
